blocks.text: Lots and land in Sperling-Duthie
Fee-simple lots

items.t: Lot character: almost entirely detached single-family housing, most of it freehold; stock ranges from modest post-war bungalows on the flatter western streets to large custom and estate-style homes in Buckingham Heights on the slope above Deer Lake. Lots on the Buckingham Heights slope are among Burnaby's larger residential lots, many with lake, mountain or city views; the balance of the area has standard Burnaby lot sizes. No numeric lot-size range is stated and none is invented here; a specific lot's dimensions: Not verified.

Heritage fabric on the lots: Sperling Avenue fronting Deer Lake Park lies within the Deer Lake Park Heritage Precinct, where the City's heritage register lists early-1900s houses such as the Woodward House at 5195 Sperling Avenue (built 1912) — heritage review is part of the lot diligence on that frontage, not a separate land category.

Serviced position: the research states no servicing position for individual lots; a 2026 utility dollar figure: Not verified. Septic or well use: Not verified. Confirm servicing for the specific parcel with the City.
ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Sperling-Duthie is confirmed and no split is stated — ALR status is a per-parcel check on ALC mapping.

Hazard note, as documented: the Burnaby Lake Park Association warns that the Sperling Avenue/Sprott Street park frontage has no established sidewalks and the road will flood after heavy rainfall (community association source); parcel-level floodplain status for individual Sperling-Duthie lots: Not verified, and no flood zone from any other city's ledger is imported here.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Sperling-Duthie

items.t: Sperling-Duthie is a central-Burnaby residential area around Sperling Avenue and Duthie Avenue, west and north of Deer Lake, crossed by Canada Way; Buckingham Heights — the prestige pocket on the slope east of Deer Lake — sits within/adjacent to this sub-area, and nearby areas are Deer Lake, Burnaby Lake, Cascade Heights, Brentwood Park, and Metrotown to the south. The board sub-area name is "Sperling-Duthie" (as used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby).

Deer Lake Park borders the sub-area: its trails connect the lake with the Burnaby Art Gallery, the Shadbolt Centre for the Arts, Burnaby Village Museum and Hart House restaurant; the park's main address is 6450 Deer Lake Avenue with access from Sperling Avenue. The section of boardwalk by the Deer Lake boat launch is closed from September 21, 2026 for a full replacement, with completion scheduled by winter 2027 and a signed detour via Sperling Avenue and Deer Lake Drive.

Burnaby City Hall is at 4949 Canada Way, just west of the sub-area; Burnaby Hospital (3935 Kincaid Street, Fraser Health) is just south of Canada Way, in a multi-phase redevelopment including a new six-storey pavilion with 83 beds in Phase 1 (2021–2026).

Transit: Sperling Avenue's north end is served by Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station, an elevated Millennium Line station at Sperling Avenue and Lougheed Highway, with bus routes 110, 134 and 144 connecting there — the 144 running between Metrotown Station and SFU. Burnaby Lake Regional Park wraps the lake immediately north of Lougheed Highway, walkable from the station.

Schools (SD41, Ministry-listed names only): École Sperling Elementary (2200 Sperling Avenue) is the in-area elementary school on Sperling Avenue itself; Burnaby Central Secondary (6011 Deer Lake Parkway) is the secondary school located in the Deer Lake/Central Burnaby area. Catchment is address-based: the one settled SD41 locator run documented — for the single sample address 2200 Sperling Avenue only — returns Sperling Elementary (K–7) / Burnaby North Secondary (8–12); Burnaby Central is NOT the catchment secondary for that address, and the settled schools position also holds that Montecito is NOT Sperling catchment. The full street-by-street split across the sub-area is not verified.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Sperling-Duthie

items.t: OCP — Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan: adopted December 9, 2025; it replaces the 1998 OCP Bylaw, and its land use map takes precedence over older neighbourhood community plan maps where they conflict. Review the 2050 OCP land use map before assuming density or subdivision potential on a large lot.

Zoning — Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026, No. 14815: adopted June 9, 2026 and in effect July 1, 2026 (never the former 1965 No. 4742). Burnaby consolidated its former single- and two-family districts into one R1 Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) District in June 2024 — R1 lots may hold 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop, and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified.

Subdivision + servicing — HELD not confirmed: Burnaby's servicing bylaw base number is not confirmed (an Amendment 14667, 2024 is on record, but the base number is not adopted here). (Standing ledger position.)

Heritage precinct: properties on Sperling Avenue fronting Deer Lake Park sit in the Deer Lake Park Heritage Precinct with heritage-register listings — check the register and precinct requirements before planning renovations or a rebuild on that frontage.

ALR rules (for completeness — no Sperling-Duthie ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR, and no flat line is asserted for this area.

blocks.text: Good to know about Sperling-Duthie

items.t: Every "Sperling-Duthie" search result needs an address check against the Deer Lake / Canada Way geography before it is priced as this area.

The lake-end and station-end of the same sub-area sell on different things: homes toward Sperling Avenue's north end can honestly be sold on walking access to Sperling–Burnaby Lake Station and the Burnaby Lake trail network, while Deer Lake-end homes sell on the park, the heritage precinct and lot size — the transit claim does not stretch to the lake end.

The boardwalk a buyer walks at a showing is mid-replacement: the Deer Lake boat-launch boardwalk section closed September 21, 2026 for a full replacement, completing by winter 2027, with the signed detour running via Sperling Avenue and Deer Lake Drive — a dated, temporary condition, not a permanent loss of the trail network.

Buckingham Heights lot size is the sub-area's real land premium: the research records the slope lots above Deer Lake as among Burnaby's larger residential lots, many with lake, mountain or city views — the premium is documented as lot size and view, not as any subdivision potential, and the new R1 stratification permission is what is starting to matter on the biggest lots.
